text:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout completed step 'canary-traffic' for release v3.4.1 -> eu-satellite. Smoke probes: 2/6 hosts reporting kv-cache-warmup latency > 2s, failing threshold. Auto-fallback not triggered because 4/6 clear. 

marta: saw the alert. is this a transient warmup noise or something deeper? which hosts?

samir: hosts eu-sat-03 and eu-sat-06. I pulled the probe logs, paste below. seems tied to prefix cache misses during first requests after start.

samir: ```
[2026-02-18T09:34:12Z] host=eu-sat-03 probe=kv-warmup latency=2310ms miss_rate=78% model=redwood-13b variant=q4
[2026-02-18T09:34:13Z] host=eu-sat-06 probe=kv-warmup latency=2475ms miss_rate=81% model=redwood-13b variant=q4
[2026-02-18T09:34:14Z] host=eu-sat-01 probe=kv-warmup latency=420ms miss_rate=12%
```

jen: curious — those hosts were part of the staggered warmstart group. Did the deploybot trigger a warmstart on them?

samir: looks like warmstart happened but KV prefetch didn't complete before first probes. possibly upstream network jitter to kv-store or cold disk read.

ryan: can we run a manual quickcheck to force prefix prefetch and re-run the smoke for just those two hosts? if that fixes, we can continue rollout. I don't want a full rollback yet.

marta: agree. options: 1) pause rollout and re-run targeted prefetch + recheck, 2) pin traffic away from eu-satellite and continue elsewhere, 3) full rollback to v3.4.0. I'm leaning to pause + targeted fix.

jen: how long for manual prefetch? I can trigger a synthetic that warms the common prefixes in ~30s.

samir: give me 30s, I'll run the warmup script: `./tools/kv_warmup --hosts eu-sat-03,eu-sat-06 --prefix-file common_prefixes.txt`

deploy-bot: Manual intervention flagged by marta. Pausing progressive rollout for 12 minutes. Canary pinned at 40% for unaffected hosts.

oncall-bot: Incident watch created: #INC-2026-0723 (eu-satellite-warmup). Severity: low. Owner: samir.

samir: warmup triggered. running smoke again in 45s.

samir: ```
$ curl -s -X POST https://smoke.redwood.internal/run -d '{"targets": ["eu-sat-03","eu-sat-06"], "probe":"kv-warmup" }'
response: ok. results in 3m
```

samir: rerun done: eu-sat-03 latency=380ms miss_rate=9%, eu-sat-06 latency=410ms miss_rate=11%. back to nominal.

ryan: nice. any persistent errors in the host logs? CPU/mem or IO spikes?

samir: no CPU/mem. there was a brief disk read queue uptick at 09:33:40Z correlated with a storage maintenance job in that AZ. looks like a coincident timing issue.

marta: based on that, I'm going to resume rollout but keep canary gates stricter for eu-satellite for next 30m. if we see >1 host fail again we pin and roll back.

deploy-bot: Rollout resumed at 1764701110. New gating: eu-satellite stricter thresholds (kv-warmup latency 1.5s), probe interval increased to 60s for 30m.

jen: i'll update release notes with the post-deploy check steps and the mitigation we used. quick blurb: "eu-satellite transient KV warmup spike during warmstart; manual rewarm and stricter gating applied; no rollback needed."

marta: thanks. tagging infra to monitor storage job scheduling so we don't collide with warmstarts next time. :handshake:

oncall-bot: #INC-2026-0723 status -> resolved (mitigated, observation window active until 30m).
